div.div: Everything before this point was about reaching the target. This is what happens once you can: three ways to drive the attacks, one status chain, and a report that ends in a policy recommendation.

div.span:
Over 500 curated attack scenarios,
refreshed every two weeks from
OWASP LLM Top 10, MITRE ATLAS,
NIST AI RMF and DASF V2.0.
About five hours.
The first scan on any target. It is
the baseline every later run is
compared against.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 424px; height: 1px; padding-top: 123px; margin-left: 487px;

div.span:
An attack agent that adapts: it reads
each answer and writes the next
prompt from what it learned.
Duration depends on the parameters.
Black box with no detail, grey box with
the use case and goals, white box with
the system prompt. More context in
means more targeted attacks out.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 424px; height: 1px; padding-top: 123px; margin-left: 957px;

div.span:
Your own prompts, uploaded as CSV
or through the API.
As long as the prompt count takes.
For the scenarios nobody else has:
a compliance obligation specific to
the industry, a brand rule, or a
regression set built from last
quarter's findings.

div.div:
FAILED or ABORTED
the whole run, or stopped by hand

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 518px; height: 1px; padding-top: 375px; margin-left: 863px;

div.div: Watch RUNNING, not the end. Error logs are readable in real time, so a configuration mistake shows up in the first few minutes rather than five hours later. A run that drifts toward PARTIALLY_COMPLETE is usually a rate limit or a guardrail code that was never configured, and both are fixable before the next attempt.

Higher means more vulnerable.
Composite, derived from the
Attack Success Rate.
Aim for 0 to 25.

The share of attacks that got the

Aim for under 5 percent, and
for zero critical findings.

div.span:
Critical remediate immediately
High remediate before production
Medium plan it, monitor in the meantime
Low track and pick up later
Grouped by the four categories:
Security, Safety, Compliance, Brand.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 314px; height: 1px; padding-top: 569px; margin-left: 1067px;

display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.span:
An AI-written summary, plus runtime
security policy recommendations that
can be applied directly in AIRS.
This is the step that turns a test
result into a control, and the one
worth walking the customer through
rather than emailing.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1378px; height: 1px; padding-top: 740px; margin-left: 3px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #666666;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #666666; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Drill-down differs by scan type: a static run exposes each attack prompt, the reply, the verdict and the severity, and the full thread for a multi-turn attack. A dynamic run exposes the complete conversation between the attack agent and the target, stream by stream.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 664px; height: 1px; padding-top: 791px; margin-left: 17px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #00294D;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #00294D; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.b: Select every category on the first run

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 648px; height: 1px; padding-top: 811px; margin-left: 19px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Security carries 10 subcategories and belongs in every scan.
Safety matters for anything customer-facing or regulated.
Compliance maps to OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, NIST and DASF V2.
Brand applies to public-facing and branded experiences.
Run all four the first time and narrow afterwards. A baseline
taken across everything is what makes the second scan
meaningful, and narrowing later costs nothing. Narrowing first
means there is nothing to compare against.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 664px; height: 1px; padding-top: 791px; margin-left: 717px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #00294D;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #00294D; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.b: Quota is counted separately for each scan type

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 648px; height: 1px; padding-top: 811px; margin-left: 719px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Static, dynamic and custom each have their own allocated,
unlimited and consumed figures. Running out of dynamic quota
halfway through an engagement does not show up until a scan
refuses to start.
Check it at the beginning and plan the engagement against it,
rather than discovering the ceiling on the day. A five-hour
Attack Library run also means a scan started late in the day
finishes without anyone watching it.
